The word of God and then informing him of his safety, and what is meant by that: conveying the messages of God, and establishing the argument against him, and this may not be completed without It is through his interpretation of it that the argument is established, and with it the opposition is answered, and the obligatory thing cannot be completed without it, then it is obligatory.
It is known that the statement of those who think that the command to perform jihad abrogates the command to argue is absolutely invalid.

The fourth aspect: If the speaker says: The verse of arguing with the infidels - or any other thing that he claims to have abrogated - is abrogated by the verse of the sword, he will be told: What What do you mean by the verse of the sword? Do you mean a specific verse, or do you mean every verse that contains the command to jihad?
If he wanted the first, his answer would be from two angles: One of them: that the verses in which jihad is mentioned are multiple, so it is not permissible to specify Some of them.
And if he said: I mean the Almighty’s saying: {So when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them} [At-Tawbah: 5].

It was said to him: This is about fighting the polytheists, and he said after that about fighting the People of the Book: {Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Day of Resurrection. And they do not forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden, nor do they follow the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture, until they pay the tribute out of hand, and they are in disdain.} [Repentance: 29].
If the verse about the sword had been only one, this would not have been better than this, even if he said: Every verse in which there is mention of jihad.

It was said to him: Jihad was initiated in stages. The first thing that God Almighty revealed regarding it was permission, saying: “Permission is given to those who fight because they have been wronged.” And indeed, God has power to help them.} [Al-Hajj: 39].

More than one of the scholars has mentioned that this is the first verse revealed regarding jihad, and after that its obligation was revealed by saying: {It is decreed upon you Fighting} [Al-Baqarah: 216].

And they were not commanded to fight those who asked for peace with them. Rather, He said: {Then if they turn back, seize them and kill them wherever you find them, and do not take from them a guardian. And no helper - except those who join a people between whom and you there is a covenant - or who come to you with their hearts determined not to fight you or fight their people - And if God had willed, He would have given them authority over you, and they would have fought you. But if they separated from you and did not fight you, and offered you peace, then God has not made for you a way over them. [An-Nisa: 89-90]
Likewise, those who made a truce with them were not commanded to fight him, even if the truce was a permissible and not obligatory contract.

Then he revealed in Bara’ah the command to abandon covenants, and commanded them to fight all polytheists, and commanded them to fight the People of the Book if they did not They will submit until they pay the tribute by hand while they are young, and it is not permissible for them to abandon fighting them even if they make peace with them and make an absolute truce with them. The possibility of their jihad.

If he said: The sign of the sword that nullified the argument is the sign of permission. It was said: The verse of permission was revealed at the beginning of his introduction to Medina, before he sent any of the companies, and he argued after these infidels.

The same applies if it is said: verses enjoining fighting. It was said: His saying: “Fighting is prescribed for you” [Al-Baqarah: 216]. It was first revealed before Badr, and there is no doubt that jihad was obligatory on the day of Uhud, the Trench, the conquest of Khaybar and Mecca, and God has mentioned The verses enjoining jihad in these battles, as mentioned in Surat Al Imran and Al-Ahzab. And if it is said: Rather, argumentation has only been abrogated when it was commanded to struggle against those who are at peace and against those who are not at peace, it is said:

This is invalid, for if the argument is incompatible with jihad, then it is incompatible with its permissibility and its obligation, even for a peaceful person, and if it does not contradict jihad, it does not contradict it. It contradicts the obligation of jihad for peaceful people, just as it does not contradict the obligation of jihad on others. The peaceful person may not argue or argue, or he may argue and not wrestle, just as someone else may argue and argue, and he may do one of them.

If his response to the jihad of the warrior who initiates the fighting does not negate his argument with him, then the jihad of the one who does not initiate the fighting does not negate the It is better and more appropriate to argue with him, because he who is farthest from fighting is less hostile to fighting than he who is the greatest fighter. This is explained by: The fifth aspect: which is to say:

What is abrogated is to limit oneself to argument. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was initially commanded to struggle with the infidels with his tongue, not with his tongue. With his hand, he calls them and exhorts them and argues with them in a way that is best and fights against them with the Qur’an a great struggle. God Almighty said in Surah Al-Furqan: And it is Meccan: {And if We had willed, We could certainly have sent into every town a warner - so obey not the disbelievers, and fight them therein with a great struggle} [Al-Furqan: 51-52].

He was commanded to stop fighting them due to his inability and the inability of the Muslims to do so. Then, when he migrated to Medina and had helpers there He was given permission to engage in jihad, then when they gained strength, it was prescribed for them to fight, but it was not prescribed for them to fight those who were at peace with them. Because they could not bear to fight all the infidels.

When God conquered Mecca and the fighting of the Quraysh, the Arab kings, ceased, and Arab delegations came to him with Islam, God Almighty commanded him to fight the infidels. All of them except the one who had a temporary covenant, and he ordered him to renounce absolute covenants, and the one who removed it and abrogated it was abandoning fighting.
As for struggling against the infidels with the tongue, it is still permissible from the beginning of the matter to the end.

For if he initiated their jihad with the hand, then with the tongue is more appropriate. The Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: “Strive the polytheists with your own hands.” And your tongues and your wealth.”

He used to set up a pulpit for Hassan in his mosque in which he would struggle against the polytheists with his tongue, a jihad of sarcasm, and this was after the revelation of the verses of battle. Where is the benefit of satire compared to the benefit of establishing evidence and proofs of the validity of Islam, and invalidating the arguments of the infidels among the polytheists? And the People of the Book?

The sixth aspect: It is known that fighting was only prescribed out of necessity, and if the people had believed in the proof and signs, there would not have been a need for it. Fighting, as explaining the verses and proofs of Islam is absolutely and fundamentally obligatory.
As for jihad: it is permissible out of necessity, so how can this be an obstacle to that?

If it is said: Islam’s signs and signs have appeared, then there is no longer any need for its signs to be revealed, rather it needs the sword. It was said: It is known that God promised to make all religion apparent, the manifestation of knowledge and explanation, the manifestation of the sword and the teeth, so God Almighty said: {It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religions, even though the polytheists hate it.} [At-Tawbah: 33].

The scholars have explained his appearance with this and that, and the word “manifestation” refers to both of them, for the appearance of guidance through knowledge and clarification, and the appearance Religion is by hand and work, and God Almighty sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth. To make it prevail over all religion.

It is known that the emergence of Islam was through knowledge and clarification before its appearance by hand and fighting. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stayed in Mecca for thirteen years, demonstrating Islam with knowledge, explanation, verses, and proofs. So the Emigrants and Ansar believed in him willingly and willingly, without a sword, because of the clear signs, proofs and miracles that he showed them. Then he demonstrated it with the sword. If it is obligatory for us to wage jihad against the infidels with the sword, first and foremost, then it is obligatory for us to explain Islam. Informing it first and foremost against those who challenge it is the best and most likely way.

The obligation of this comes before the obligation of that, and its benefit comes before its benefit, and it is known that he needs the sword all the time, so it is. He is in need of knowledge and clarification, and to show him with knowledge and clarification is the same as showing him with the sword, and it is a general manifestation by which he is superior to all. A religion that, although many of the disbelievers were not defeated by its sword, likewise many people were not made clear to them by its signs and proofs. Rather, they may slander And they establish arguments for its invalidity, especially since those who are oppressed by the sword. Among them are many hypocrites, so these people strive with knowledge and clarification. Without the sword and the teeth, he confirms this:

The seventh aspect: which is that fighting is only for an oppressor, for whoever fights the Muslims is only an oppressor and an aggressor, and against whom The proof, so he opposed the Messenger after guidance had become clear to him, and he followed a path other than the path of the believers. He was nothing but an unjust.

As for the argument, it may be for an unjust person: either one who challenges the religion unjustly, or one against whom a clear argument has been established and who has refused to accept it. It may be that a person seeking guidance has a right that he has not attained.

Or to someone who has been informed of some of the signs of the prophecy of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the evidence of his prophecy, but to him this has been contradicted by contradictory suspicions. Therefore, he needed an answer to those oppositions.
Or he is seeking to know the evidence of prophecy in the manner in which this is known.
If the fighting that only takes place to repel the injustice of the combatant is lawful.
The argument that takes place to ward off his injustice and to benefit him and others is permissible in the first way.

Mujahid said: {And do not dispute with the People of the Book except in a way that is best, except with those who are unjust among them} [Al-Ankabut: 46]. He said: Those who were unjust are those who fought you and did not give you the tribute. And in another word about him, he said: Those who did wrong: among them are the people of war who have no covenant; To argue with them with the sword. In a narration from him, he said: Do not fight anyone except those who fight you and do not pay you the tribute. In a narration from him, he said: Whoever among them pays the poll tax, do not say anything to him except good. On the authority of Mujahid:
Except for what is better, and if they say evil, say good. This is a matter of Mujahid and does not make it abrogated, and this is the view of most commentators.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: {And do not argue with the People of the Book except in a way that is best} [Al-Ankabut: 46]. He said: It is not abrogated. But on the authority of Qatada, he said: It was abrogated. {So kill the polytheists wherever you find them} [At-Tawbah: 5], and there is no argument stronger than the sword.
The first is more correct; Because these are among those who did wrong, so there is no abrogation.

What is astonishing about him is that some of those who deny arguing with the infidels based on the appearance of evidence of prophecy, we find him and those of his sheikhs whom he venerated, who In the fundamentals of the religion, they rely on their view and debate, and they claim that they have established the evidence of prophecy, which they have presented from suspicions, doubts, and appeals. There are about eighty questions about the evidence of prophecy, and they answered them with answers that are not suitable as answers to speculative issues, but rather It is closer to establishing the quasi-conspirators than it is to establishing the principles of religion.

They are, as Al-Ghazali and others represented them, someone who strikes a tree and causes it to shake, while he claims that he wants to make it steady. Many of these imams are in such a state of confusion in their belief in prophecy that this is not the place to explain it, and yet they claim that it has What has become apparent among the People of the Book is what did not appear among the sheikhs of these theorists, and they forbid the revelation of God’s signs and proofs, which is the ultimate goal. The demands of their sheikhs, and they did not give them their due, either through inability or negligence.

The eighth aspect: Many of the People of the Book claim that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation established their religion by the sword, not With guidance, knowledge, and signs. When they seek knowledge and debate, it is said to them: You have no answer except the sword. This is what decides Their false belief, and this was one of the greatest arguments they used against themselves against the corruption of Islam, and that it is not the religion of a messenger from God, but it was the religion of a king who established it by the sword.

The ninth aspect: It is known that the sword, especially the sword of the Muslims and the People of the Book, is an accessory to knowledge and proof. Rather, it is a sword The polytheists are subordinate to their opinions and beliefs, and the sword is of the same type as work, and work - never - is subordinate to knowledge and opinion.

Then, explaining the religion of Islam with knowledge and showing that what contradicts it is misguidance and ignorance is confirmation of the origin of the religion of Islam. And to avoid the origin of other religions whose followers are fought over, and whenever its validity and the corruption of others become apparent, people will be one of two men: either A man to whom the truth became clear and he followed it, this is the greatest purpose of sending messengers, or a man who did not follow it, this is what it was based on. The argument is, either because he did not look into the signs of Islam, or he looked and learned and followed his own desires, or he fell short.

And when the proof is established against him, he is satisfied with God and His Messenger, and supports the sword of Islam, and is humbled by the sword of the infidels, and if it is determined that among them Whoever is unable to understand the argument, then if he is not excused for not performing it, then he is more deserving of not being excused despite its being established, even if He was excused for its standing, so he is more excused for its absence, so according to both estimates, standing up for the Hujjah is more helpful and excused, and God Almighty said: {And we were not We will punish until We send a messenger} [Al-Isra: 15].
And God Almighty said: {so that people may have no argument against God after the Messengers} [An-Nisa: 165].

And the Almighty said: {So the women whom you meet are in remembrance as an excuse or a vow} [Al-Mursalat: 5] And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no one to whom an excuse is more beloved than God, than For that reason He sent messengers bringing good tidings and warnings.”

chapters.title: A chapter from the evidence of the generality of the message of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace
paragraphs: [Chapter: From the evidence of the generality of the message of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace] [Islam Al-Najashi]

Before the story of Najran, many Jews and Christians, their leaders and others, believed in him when it became clear to them that he was a messenger. May God bless them, just as Negus, king of Abyssinia, believed in him. He and his people were Christians, and his belief in him was at the beginning of the command of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He greeted him when his companions were weak in Mecca, and the infidels were oppressing them, harming them, and punishing them for believing in God. And His Messenger, so a group of them emigrated, such as Uthman bin Affan, Abdul Rahman bin Awf, Al-Zubayr bin Al-Awwam, and Abdullah bin Masoud and Ja`far bin

chapters.title: Islam Negus
paragraphs: Abu Talib, and other men and women, and he was a just king, so the infidels sent messengers after them with gifts to return them to them. So he refused from his justice to hand them over to them until he heard their words. When he heard their words and what they told him about the matter of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, He believed in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and gave them shelter.

And when he heard the Qur’an, he said: This is what Moses brought to come out of a single niche. And when he asked them about their opinion regarding the Messiah over him Peace be upon them. They said: We bear witness that he is the servant of God and His Messenger, and the word he gave to Mary the virgin, the virgin, who had not been touched by a man. Al-Najashi said: To Ja`far bin Abi Talib: By God, Jesus, son of Mary, did not add anything more to what you said than this stick, and its companions gnawed at it, so he said:

And if you give in, even if you give in, and he sent his son and a group of his companions to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with Ja`far bin Abi Talib, and he came Jafar was killed by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the year of Khaybar. A group of scholars and scholars, such as Ahmad ibn Hanbal, mentioned their story in Al-Musnad. Ibn Saad in al-Tabaqat, Abu Nu`aym in al-Hilyah, and others, and it was mentioned by the people of interpretation, hadith, and jurisprudence, and it is frequently reported among Scientists.

Ahmad said: Yaqoub bin Ibrahim bin Saeed narrated to me, on the authority of his father, he said: Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated to us, Muhammad bin Muslim bin narrated to me. Abdullah bin Shihab Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abdul Rahman bin Al-Harith bin Hisham Al-Makhzoumi, on the authority of Umm Salamah bint Abi Umayyah bin Al-Mughirah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and may God be pleased with her, said:

When we settled in the land of Abyssinia, we had the best neighbor (Al-Najashi) as our neighbor. We believed in our religion, and we served God. We were not harmed, and we did not hear anything that we disliked. When this reached the Quraysh, they decided to send two flogged men to the Negus among us, and to give the Negus gifts of any extravagant goods. Mecca, and it was astonishing what people brought to him from there, so they gathered a lot of people for him, and they did not leave any of his penguins alone unless they were guided. A gift for him, then they sent Abdullah bin Abi Rabi’ah bin Al-Mughirah with that.

Al-Makhzoumi, and Amr bin Al-Aas bin Wael Al-Sahmi, and they gave them their orders, and said to them: Give each one his gift before it Speak to the Negus about them, then give the Negus his gifts, then ask him to hand them over to you before he speaks to them. She said: So they went out. So they approached the Negus, and we were with him in the best abode of the best neighbour. There was not a penguin of his penguins left who did not give him his gift before he They spoke to the Negus, then they said to each of them in their own way:

Indeed, some of us foolish young men have arrived in the king’s country, and they have departed from the religion of their people, and have not entered into your religion, and have come with an innovated religion that we do not know. Neither we nor you, and we have sent to the king among them the nobles of their people to return them to them. So when we speak to the king regarding them, advise him. That he should hand them over to us and not speak to them, for their people have a higher eye than them and are more knowledgeable of what they have rebuked. So they said to them: Yes, and then they approached. They gave their gifts to the Negus, who accepted them from them, then they spoke to him and said to him:

O king, some foolish young men have arrived in your country, and they have abandoned the religion of their people, and have not entered your religion, and have brought an innovated religion that is not We know it, not you, and we have sent to you among them the nobles of their people, from their fathers, uncles, and clans, to return them to them. I look up to them, and I know what they reproached them for and blamed them for.
She said: There was nothing more hateful to Abdullah bin Abi Rabia and Amr bin Al-Aas than for the Negus to hear our words.

Then his bastards around him said: They have spoken the truth, O king. Their people are more considerate of them, and more aware of what they blamed on them, so hand them over to them. Let him return them to their country and people. She said: The Negus became angry, then he said, “No, by God, by God, then I will not hand them over to them, nor will I fight people who were neighbors with me and settled in my country and chose me.” Who else should I call them and ask them what these two say about their matter? If they are as they say, I will hand them over to them and bring them back. To their people, and if they were other than that, I would protect them from both of them and be kind to them as long as they were kind to me.

She said: Then he sent to the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and summoned them. When his Messenger came to them, they gathered together and then said to one another: What do you say to a man when you come to him? They said: We say, by God, what He taught us and what our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded us to do. What is happening in that is what is happening. When they came to him, Abu Nu`aym added, and the Negus had summoned his bishops and had their Qur’ans around him. When they came to him, he asked them, and he said: What is this religion? Wherein you separated from your people and did not enter my religion or the religion of any of these nations?
She said: The one who spoke to him was Ja`far bin Abi Talib, and he said:

O king, we were a people of pre-Islamic times. We worshiped idols, ate dead animals, committed immoral acts, cut ties of kinship, and committed wrongdoing. Neighborhood, and the strong among us ate the weak, so we were like that until God sent to us a messenger from among us whose lineage, honesty, honesty, and chastity we know. So He called us to God so that we might monotheize Him and worship Him, putting off what we and our fathers had worshiped other than Him, of stones and idols, and He commanded us By telling the truth, fulfilling trustworthiness, maintaining ties of kinship, being good neighbors, abstaining from forbidden things and blood, forbidding immoral acts, and saying: falsehood, consuming the orphan’s property, slandering chaste women, commanding us to worship God not associating anything with Him, commanding us to pray and to pay zakat. And fasting.

She said: So he enumerated the matters of Islam to him, saying: So we believed him, believed in him, and followed him in what he brought, so we worshiped God alone and did not associate anything with Him.

And we forbade what was forbidden to us, and we made lawful what was lawful to us, so our people transgressed against us, torturing us and tempting us from our religion in order to return us to worship. Idols from the worship of God, and to make lawful what we used to make lawful of evil things, when they oppressed us and wronged us and made hardship to us and came between us and Our religion: We went to your country, and we chose you over everyone else, and we desired your neighbourhood, and we hoped that we would not be wronged before you, O king.
She said: Then Al-Najashi said to him: Do you have anything of what he brought from God?
She said: Jaafar said to him: Yes. Al-Najashi said to him: So read it to me. Then he recited to him part of Surat Maryam:

{كهيعص - ذِكْرُ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّكَ عَبْدَهُ زَكَرِيَّا - إِذْ نَادَى رَبَّهُ نِدَاءً خَفِيًّا - قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي وَهَنَ الْعَظْمُ مِنِّي وَاشْتَعَلَ الرَّأْسُ شَيْبًا وَلَمْ أَكُنْ بِدُعَائِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيًّا - وَإِنِّي خِفْتُ الْمَوَالِيَ مِنْ وَرَائِي وَكَانَتِ امْرَأَتِي عَاقِرًا فَهَبْ لِي مِنْ لَدُنْكَ وَلِيًّا - يَرِثُنِي وَيَرِثُ مِنْ آلِ يَعْقُوبَ وَاجْعَلْهُ رَبِّ رَضِيًّا - يَازَكَرِيَّا إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلَامٍ اسْمُهُ يَحْيَى لَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ سَمِيًّا - قَالَ رَبِّ أَنَّى يَكُونُ لِي غُلَامٌ وَكَانَتِ امْرَأَتِي عَاقِرًا وَقَدْ بَلَغْتُ مِنَ الْكِبَرِ عِتِيًّا - قَالَ كَذَلِكَ قَالَ رَبُّكَ هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ وَقَدْ خَلَقْتُكَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَلَمْ تَكُ شَيْئًا - قَالَ رَبِّ اجْعَلْ لِي آيَةً قَالَ آيَتُكَ أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ النَّاسَ ثَلَاثَ لَيَالٍ سَوِيًّا - فَخَرَجَ عَلَى قَوْمِهِ مِنَ الْمِحْرَابِ فَأَوْحَى إِلَيْهِمْ أَنْ سَبِّحُوا بُكْرَةً وَعَشِيًّا - يَايَحْيَى خُذِ الْكِتَابَ بِقُوَّةٍ وَآتَيْنَاهُ الْحُكْمَ صَبِيًّا - وَحَنَانًا مِنْ لَدُنَّا وَزَكَاةً وَكَانَ تَقِيًّا - وَبَرًّا بِوَالِدَيْهِ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ جَبَّارًا عَصِيًّا - وَسَلَامٌ عَلَيْهِ يَوْمَ وُلِدَ وَيَوْمَ يَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ يُبْعَثُ حَيًّا - وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ مَرْيَمَ إِذِ انْتَبَذَتْ مِنْ أَهْلِهَا مَكَانًا شَرْقِيًّا - فَاتَّخَذَتْ مِنْ دُونِهِمْ حِجَابًا فَأَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْهَا رُوحَنَا فَتَمَثَّلَ لَهَا بَشَرًا سَوِيًّا - قَالَتْ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِالرَّحْمَنِ مِنْكَ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَقِيًّا - قَالَ إِنَّمَا أَنَا رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ لِأَهَبَ لَكِ غُلَامًا زَكِيًّا - قَالَتْ أَنَّى يَكُونُ لِي غُلَامٌ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِي بَشَرٌ وَلَمْ أَكُ بَغِيًّا - قَالَ كَذَلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ وَلِنَجْعَلَهُ آيَةً لِلنَّاسِ وَرَحْمَةً مِنَّا وَكَانَ أَمْرًا مَقْضِيًّا - فَحَمَلَتْهُ فَانْتَبَذَتْ بِهِ مَكَانًا قَصِيًّا - فَأَجَاءَهَا الْمَخَاضُ إِلَى جِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ قَالَتْ يَالَيْتَنِي مِتُّ قَبْلَ هَذَا وَكُنْتُ نَسْيًا مَنْسِيًّا - فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا أَلَّا تَحْزَنِي قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا - وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ تُسَاقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًا جَنِيًّا - فَكُلِي وَاشْرَبِي وَقَرِّي عَيْنًا فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ مِنَ الْبَشَرِ أَحَدًا فَقُولِي إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَنِ صَوْمًا فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ الْيَوْمَ إِنْسِيًّا - فَأَتَتْ بِهِ قَوْمَهَا تَحْمِلُهُ قَالُوا يَامَرْيَمُ لَقَدْ جِئْتِ شَيْئًا فَرِيًّا - يَاأُخْتَ هَارُونَ مَا كَانَ أَبُوكِ امْرَأَ سَوْءٍ وَمَا كَانَتْ أُمُّكِ بَغِيًّا - فَأَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ قَالُوا كَيْفَ نُكَلِّمُ مَنْ كَانَ فِي الْمَهْدِ صَبِيًّا - قَالَ إِنِّي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ آتَانِيَ الْكِتَابَ وَجَعَلَنِي نَبِيًّا - وَجَعَلَنِي مُبَارَكًا أَيْنَ مَا كُنْتُ وَأَوْصَانِي بِالصَّلَاةِ وَالزَّكَاةِ مَا دُمْتُ حَيًّا - وَبَرًّا بِوَالِدَتِي وَلَمْ يَجْعَلْنِي جَبَّارًا شَقِيًّا - وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَيَّ يَوْمَ وُلِدْتُ وَيَوْمَ أَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ أُبْعَثُ حَيًّا - ذَلِكَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ قَوْلَ الْحَقِّ الَّذِي فِيهِ يَمْتَرُونَ - مَا كَانَ لِلَّهِ أَنْ يَتَّخِذَ مِنْ وَلَدٍ سُبْحَانَهُ إِذَا قَضَى أَمْرًا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ - وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ - فَاخْتَلَفَ الْأَحْزَابُ مِنْ بَيْنِهِمْ فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ مَشْهَدِ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ - أَسْمِعْ بِهِمْ وَأَبْصِرْ يَوْمَ يَأْتُونَنَا لَكِنِ الظَّالِمُونَ الْيَوْمَ فِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ - وَأَنْذِرْهُمْ يَوْمَ الْحَسْرَةِ إِذْ قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ وَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ - إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَرِثُ الْأَرْضَ وَمَنْ عَلَيْهَا وَإِلَيْنَا يُرْجَعُونَ} [مريم:

Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with her, said: By God, the Negus cried until his beard was soaked, and his bishops cried until they soaked their Qur’an when they They heard what was recited to them, then Al-Najashi said: This is what Moses brought to come out of a single niche. Then he said to Abdullah bin Abi Rabia and Amr bin Al-Aas: Go, by God, I will never hand them over to you, and I will never hand them over to you.
Umm Salamah said: When he left him, he said: Amr ibn Al-Aas, by God, I will come to him tomorrow, disgrace them in his presence, then cleanse it. Their greenness.

She said: Then Abdullah bin Abi Rabi’ah - and he was the more pious of the two men among us - said to him: Do not do it; For they have kinship, even if they differed from us. He said: By God, we would have told him that they claim that Jesus, son of Mary, is a slave.
She said: Then the next day he came upon him, and he said to him: O king, they are saying a terrible thing about Jesus, son of Mary, so send to them. So ask them what they say about it.
She said: So he sent to them asking them about him.

She said: The like of it has not been sent down to us. So the people gathered and said to one another: What do you say about Jesus if he asks you about him? They said: We say, by God, about it, what God said, and what our Prophet brought, and what is happening in that, so when they entered upon it, he said to them: What is happening? You say about Jesus, son of Mary, so Ja`far bin Abi Talib said to him: We say about him what our Prophet brought: He is the servant of God, His Messenger, and His Spirit. And his word he delivered to Mary, the virgin.

She said: Then the Negus hit his hand on the ground and took a stick from it, then said: Jesus, son of Mary, did not say anything except this stick, so she snorted. I was confused about him when he said what he said, so he said: And if you do, by God, go, for you are the people of my land - and the people are the safe ones - those who curse you. He will be fined, then he who reviles you will be fined, then he who reviles you will be fined, so I do not like to have gold behind my back, even though I have harmed a man of you - and the back is in the language of the Abyssinians:

Al-Jabal - Return their gifts to them, so we have no need of them. By God, God did not take a bribe from me when He restored my kingdom to me, so he took the bribe. In it, and whatever people obey about me, I obey them in it.
She said: So they left from him in disgrace, and what they had brought was returned to them, and we resided with him in the best house with the best neighbours.
She said: By God, we are upon that when it was revealed. Meaning: someone who disputes with him over his kingdom.

She said: By God, we have never known a grief greater than our grief at that time. We feared that this would appear on the Negus and he would come. A man who does not know what Al-Najashi knew from us.

Abdullah bin Aamir bin Al-Zubayr narrated on the authority of his father, who said: When his enemy Al-Najashi descended from his land, the immigrants came and said: We We will go out to them, and we will fight with you, and you will see our reward, and we will reward you for what you did to us. He said: The one whom God helps is better than the one whom God helps. The people say: The one whom God helps is better than the one whom the people support, but he refused to do that to them.

(We returned to) the hadith of Umm Salamah, who said: Al-Najashi walked and between them was the width of the Nile. She said: Then the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Who A man goes out to attend the battle of the people and then brings us the news?
She said: Al-Zubayr bin Al-Awwam said: I am.

She said: He was one of the youngest people in age. She said: So we blew a skin for him and he placed it on his chest and then swam on it until he went out to the side of the Nile. The place where the people met. Then he set off until he met them.
She said: We prayed to God for Negus to prevail over his enemy and give him strength in his country.

She said: By God, we are probably anticipating this for what is going to happen, when Al-Zubayr appeared running and waving his garment and saying: Have you not given good news? He has appeared. Al-Najashi, may God destroy his enemy.
By God, I have never known a joy like it.

She said: The Negus returned, and God had destroyed his enemy, and given him strength in his country, and the affairs of Abyssinia had been entrusted to him, so we were in good condition with him. A house until we came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
The entirety of this story was narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan from the hadith of Abu Musa.

And in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu Musa, he said: We reached the departure of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while we were in Yemen, so we left, migrating to him. And two brothers of mine, the youngest of whom I am, are fifty-two men from my people. So we boarded a ship and our ship delivered to the Negus in Abyssinia. So Ja'far bin Abi Talib and his companions agreed with him. Ja'far said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent us and ordered us - meaning By residence - so stay with us. He said: So we stayed with him until we all came. He said:

So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, agreed with us when he conquered Khaybar, and he shared some of it for us. He did not swear to anyone who was absent from the conquest of Khaybar except us. For those who testified with us, the owners of our ship, along with Jafar and his companions, a share will be given to them along with them.

He said: When he saw some of the people saying to us - meaning the people of the ship - we preceded you in migration, he said: Asma bint Umays entered - and she was among those who He came with us - Hafsa was a visitor, and she had migrated to the Negus among those who migrated to him, so Omar entered to see Hafsa and Asma was with her, and he said When Omar saw Asma: Who is this? She said: Asma bint Umays, and Omar said: This Ethiopian woman? This navy? Asmaa said: Yes, then Omar said: We preceded you in the migration, we have more right to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so she got angry and said:

O Omar, no, by God, you were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, feeding your hungry and advising your ignorant, and we were in a land of hatred and hostility. In Abyssinia, and that is in God, Blessed and Most High, and in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and by God I do not eat food or drink anything until I remember what you said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. We were being harmed and afraid, and I will mention that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And I ask him, and by God, I will not lie, deviate, or add to that.

When the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, came, she said: O Messenger of God, Omar said such-and-such. The Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: “So what? Did you tell him? She said: I said such-and-such. He said: He has no more right to me than you. He and his companions have one migration, and you, the people of the ship, have two migrations. .

She said: I saw Abu Musa and the people of the ship coming to me with messengers asking me about this hadith. There is nothing in this world that I am happy about. There is nothing greater in their souls than what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said.
Abu Burdah said: Asmaa said: I saw Abu Musa, and he would like to recall this hadith from me. They included it in the two Sahihs of Bukhari. And a Muslim.

They narrated in the two Sahih books on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mourned for them the Negus, the companion of Abyssinia, on the day he died.
He said: Ask forgiveness for your brother.

On his authority, may God be pleased with him, he said: “The Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, mourned the Negus on the day he died, and said: Ask forgiveness for your brother, then he went out with the people to He prayed, so they lined up behind him, and he prayed over him and said “Allahu Akbar” four times. They took him out.

Jabir bin Abdullah, may God be pleased with them, said: “The Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, prayed for Ashamah al-Najashi, and he said four takbirs for him.” He included it in the two Sahih books.

chapters.title: Islam is one of the Arab Christians who converted to Islam
paragraphs: [Islam of the Arab Christians who converted to Islam]

Chapter: “The first time that God Almighty sent down the revelation to him, may God bless him and grant him peace, was that Khadija, his wife, presented his matter to a great scholar of A Christian scholar called Waraqah bin Nawfal, and he was one of the Christianized Arabs. He said: This is the law that Moses bin Imran used to bring. I wish I were there when your people expel you. Meaning: I wish I were young, for he was an old man, and his sight had failed. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Or are my directors? He said:
Yes, no one has ever brought anything like what you have brought except come back to me, and if your day overtakes me, I will support you with a strong victory.” Narrated by the companions of Sahih.

And a group of Christians from the People of the Book came to him in Mecca, and they believed in him, but the polytheists harmed them, so they were patient and endured his harm, so he revealed God is among them: {Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it believe in it - and when it is recited to them, they say, “We believe in it. It is the truth from our Lord. Before him were Muslims - those will be given their reward twice, because they were patient, and they avert evil with good, and spend out of what We have provided them - and when They heard the idle talk, turned away from it, and said, “Our deeds are ours, and your deeds are yours. Peace be upon you. We do not seek the ignorant.” [Al-Qasas: 52-55].

Al-Bayhaqi narrated in the book Evidence of Prophethood and Signs of the Message, saying: Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz informed us, Abu Al-Abbas informed us. Muhammad ibn Yaqoub informed us Ahmad ibn Abdul Jabbar informed us Yunus on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:

Then twenty Christians came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Mecca or near that - when news of him emerged in Abyssinians, and they found him in the assembly, so they spoke to him and asked him, and men from Quraysh were in their clubs around the Kaaba, so when they finished questioning them, The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to God, and he recited the Qur’an to them. When they heard it, their eyes overflowed with tears, then they responded to him and believed in him. They believed him, and learned from him what was described to them in their book regarding his matter, so when they got up from him, Abu Jahl confronted them with a group of Quraysh. They said:

May God let you down from a group of people whom He has sent behind you from among your own religion. You will go to them and bring them the news of the man, but your gatherings were not reassured. He was with him until you abandoned your religion and believed what he told you. We do not know of anyone more foolish than you. Or as he said to them, and they said: Peace be upon you. We do not ignore you. We have our works and you have your works. We do not wish for ourselves anything but good. And it is said - And God knows best - these verses were revealed about them:

chapters.title: Sending messengers to all the sects existing during his reign
paragraphs: {Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it believe in it} [Al-Qasas: 52] to His saying: {We do not seek the ignorant} [Al-Qasas: 55].
[Sending messengers to all the sects existing during his reign]
When it was after the year of Hudaybiyyah and the truce with the Quraysh, he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, sent his messengers to all the sects, so he sent to the Christians:

Christians of the Levant and Egypt, so he sent to Heraclius, the king of the Romans. It has been said that this Heraclius is the one to whom the Christians added ten days of fasting. During the days when the Romans and Persians fought, and he killed the Jews after he had secured them, the Christians asked him to kill them and guaranteed that he would They expiate his sin by adding to his fasting, and the Persians were Magi, and the Romans were Christians, and the Magi were the Persians who defeated the Christians first, and it was This occurred at the beginning of the mission of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Mecca and his followers were few, so the polytheists rejoiced at the victory of the Persians. Because they are closer to them, so Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, entered the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him of the victory. Persians against the Romans, so God Almighty revealed:

{M - The Romans were defeated - in the nearest part of the earth, and after they were defeated they will be defeated - in a few years. To Allah belongs the matter before and after, and on that day. The believers rejoice in God’s victory} [Al-Rum: 1-5].

This was what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was informed of before it happened, so it was as he was informed, and when Abu Bakr al-Siddiq mentioned it, he was satisfied By God, they denied him, but Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, bet on them, as mentioned by the commentators and hadith scholars. Sunaid said in his interpretation - He is the sheikh of Al-Bukhari - Hajjaj told us on the authority of Ibn Abi Al-Zinad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Urwa ibn Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Nayyar ibn Makram Al-Aslami, That he said: When God revealed to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace {Al-M - the Romans were defeated} [Al-Rum: 1-2]

To his saying {And He is the Mighty, the Most Merciful} [Al-Rum: 5] Abu Bakr came out and was reciting it in Mecca, raising his voice with it: {Al-M - the Romans have been defeated - in The closest of the earth, and they, after their defeat, will be defeated in a few years} [Al-Rum: 1-3].

Then the heads of the people of Mecca said to him: What is this, Ibn Abi Quhafa? Perhaps it is something that your friend brings. He said: No, by God, but it is the word of God. And He, Blessed and Most High, said, They said: That is between us and you if the Romans conquer Persia in a few years, so Abu Bakr bet with them, so God granted victory. The Romans conquered Persia for less than nine days, and at that time many of the polytheists converted to Islam.

Ibn Makram said: The Quraysh were only attacking on that day with horses; Because they and they are people who deny the Resurrection and people of idols, and the believers were only fighting on that day with the Romans. Because they and they are people of prophecy and belief in the resurrection, so God Almighty revealed: {And on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of God. Whoever He wills} [Al-Rum: 4].

This hadith was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi in his collection, and he said: Muhammad bin Ismail narrated to us, Ismail bin Uwais narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi narrated to me. Al-Zinad, on the authority of Abu Al-Zinad, on the authority of Urwa bin Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Nayyar bin Makram Al-Aslami, he said: When it was revealed: {Al-M - the Romans were defeated - in the lowest part of the earth And after their defeat they will be defeated - in a few years} [Al-Rum: 1-4]. On the day this verse was revealed, Persia was subjugating the Romans, and the Muslims loved the Romans to prevail over them because they and they were people. A book.
That is what God Almighty says: “And on that day the believers will rejoice - with the help of God. He helps whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Most Merciful” [Al-Rum: 4-5].

The Quraysh liked the appearance of Persia. Because they and they are neither People of the Book nor believe in a resurrection. When God revealed this verse, Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, left. It is shouted in the outskirts of Mecca: {Al-M - the Romans have been defeated - in the nearest part of the earth, and after they have been defeated they will be defeated - in a few years. To Allah belongs the matter before. And after that} [Al-Rum: 1-4].

Some people from Quraysh said to Abu Bakr: This is between us and you. Your friend claimed that the Romans will defeat Persia in a few years. Shall we not bet with you on That? Abu Bakr and the polytheists took a mortgage, and the Romans conquered Persia within a few years, and at that time many of the polytheists converted to Islam.

Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan, authentic, and strange hadith. We do not know it except from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad - meaning it is strange in this respect. Otherwise, it is well-known and narrated by the people of interpretation, mysteries, hadith, and jurisprudence, and the story is narrated by the people.

Abu Ja`far bin Jarir said in his interpretation: On the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Amra, on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that He said: The Muslims wanted the Romans to defeat Persia. Because they are People of the Book, and the polytheists would love for you to defeat the people of Persia. Because they are people of idols, he said, so they mentioned that to Abu Bakr, so Abu Bakr mentioned it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God revealed: {M - The Romans have been defeated - in the lowest part of the earth, and after their defeat they will be defeated - in a few years. To Allah belongs the matter before and after, and on that day He will rejoice. The believers} [Al-Rum: 1-4].

So Abu Bakr mentioned it to the polytheists, and they said: Set a term between us and you, and if they are defeated, then such-and-such is yours, and if they are defeated, then this-and-so is yours. Such and such, so they set a period of five years between them. “Then Abu Bakr mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to him: Would you please be careful? Did you make it less than ten? Saeed bin Jubayr said: And the “bad’” means less than ten. He said, “Then the Romans were defeated, then they were defeated. That is His saying: ‘Al-M - the Romans were defeated’ [Al-Rum: 1-2].

This was also narrated by Al-Tirmidhi: Al-Hussein bin Harith narrated to us, Muawiyah bin Amr narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Amra, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he said: This is a good, authentic, strange hadith. We only know it from a hadith Sufyan Al-Thawri, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Amra.
He also narrated it from the hadith of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ubayd Allah bin Abdullah bin Utbah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he said this is a strange hadith from this. The face.
He also narrated it from the hadith of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Atiyya, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, and he said: This is a good and strange hadith from this perspective.

A group of scholars said that the news came of the appearance of the Romans against Persia on the day of Badr, and others said that it was the day of Hudaybiyyah. This is correct, and Heraclius had walked, thanking God, from Homs to the Holy House when he had given him victory over the Persians, and the letter of the Prophet received him, may God bless him and grant him peace. May God bless him and grant him peace, calling him to Islam after God’s victory for the Romans over Persia, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers with him rejoiced.

Biographers said: When the Romans were victorious, and Heraclius, the Roman king, left his home in Homs, walking on his feet to the Holy House, giving thanks. To God Almighty when He returned to him what He had returned so that he might pray there. When he went to the Holy House and prayed there, the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was presented to him. Peace be upon him, along with Dihya al-Kalbi, inviting him to Islam.
Ibn Ishaq said: Al-Zuhri told me, on the authority of Ubayd Allah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Masoud, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas, he said: Abu Sufyan told me, he said:

We were a merchant people, and the war between us and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, besieged us until our property was destroyed. The truce between us and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace - meaning the one that was concluded on the day of Hudaybiyyah - and when the truce was concluded, we were secure, so I went out in A group of Quraysh merchants went to the Levant, and he was our main shop when Heraclius appeared on the Persians who were opposing him, and expelled them. From it, and his greatest cross was taken from him, while they had robbed him of it, so when that reached him from them and it informed him that his cross had been saved for him, Homs was his home, so he left on his feet, thanking God Almighty when He responded to him for what he responded to. To pray in the Holy House, and the path was spread out for him with carpets and the winds blew over it. So when he reached Elia and performed his prayer there and with him His patriarchs and bishops, he said:
The letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was presented to him.

He greeted with Dihya bin Khalifa Al-Kalbi in it: “In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, from Muhammad, the Messenger of God, to Heraclius, the Great of Rome, peace be upon Whoever follows guidance, as for what follows: then submit and you will be safe, and submit. God will give you your reward twice, but if you turn back, then upon you is the sin of the Arisians.” It means the generous ones.

Ibn Ishaq said, and Ibn Shihab said: The bishop of the Christians told me in the time of Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan. He claimed to me that he realized that from The command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the command and mind of Heraclius. He said: When the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was presented to him with Dihya took it and put it on his side, then he wrote to a man in Rome who was reading from the Hebrew what he was reading, mentioning his situation to him. And he describes his situation to him and tells him what came of it. He said:

Then the ruler of Rome wrote to him that he is the prophet we are waiting for, there is no doubt about him, so he followed him and believed him. So Heraclius ordered the Roman patriarchs to gather. He had his kingdom in Daskra, and he ordered that its gates be opened to them, then he looked at them from an upper room, and he feared for himself, and said: O community of Romans, I have gathered you together for good. A letter from this man has come to me inviting me to...

His religion, and he - by God - is the man whom we have been waiting for and found in our books, so come, let us follow him, let us believe him, and he will hand over our world to us. And you delayed us, so they gave the grunt of one man, then they quickly went to the gates of the prison to leave, and they found that they had been closed before them. He said: They attacked me, and he feared they would harm himself, so they attacked him, and he said:

O community of Romans, I only told you this statement that I told you; In order to see how you have steadfastly adhered to your religion because of this matter that has happened, I saw among you the one with whom I was pleased, and they fell down in prostration, and he ordered the doors to be opened. The gate was opened for them and they set off.

This is a famous hadith, from the hadith of Muhammad bin Ishaq, and he has knowledge and insight in this matter. He memorized what no one else memorized. Ibn Ishaq: And Heraclius took the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and put it on a golden reed, and held it with him in veneration. For him. This story is famous and mentioned by the companions of Sahih books.

In Al-Bukhari and Muslim, and the context is by Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, he said: Ubayd Allah ibn Abdullah ibn Utba ibn Masoud informed me that Abdullah bin Abbas told him that Abu Sufyan bin Harb told him that Heraclius was sent to him in a group of Quraysh, who were merchants in the Levant. During the period when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made peace with Abu Sufyan bin Harb and the infidels of Quraysh, they brought him while he was Elijah. So he called them to his council, and around him were the great Romans, then he called them to the translator, and he said:

Which of you is closest in lineage to this man who claims to be a prophet? Abu Sufyan said: So I said: I am the closest of them in lineage, so he said: Come closer to him. And bring his companions near, and put them at his back. Then he said to his interpreter: I will ask this man about this man. If he tells me a lie. So they lied to him. Abu Sufyan said: By God, if it were not for the shame that they would influence me to lie, I would have lied to him. Then he was the first thing he asked me. About him, he said: What is his lineage among you? I said: He is among us a relative. He said: Has any of you ever said this before? I said: No. He said: Were any of his fathers kings? I said: No.

He said: Did the noble people follow him or the weak ones? I said: Rather, their weak ones. He said: Will they increase or decrease? I said: Rather, they increase. He said: Will any of them backslide out of dissatisfaction with his religion after he enters it? I said: No. He said: Were you accusing him of lying before he said what he said? I said: No. He said: Does he betray? I said: No, and we are with him for a period of time and we do not know what he will do. He said: I could not find a word in which I could include anything other than this word. He said: Did you fight him? I said. Yes. He said: How was your fight with him? I said:

The war between us and him is a dispute that harms us and we harm him. He said: What does he command you to do? I said: He says, “Worship God alone and do not associate anything with Him, and leave what your fathers say,” and He commands us to pray, tell the truth, chastity, and ties. So he said to the translator: Tell him: I asked you about his lineage, and you mentioned that he is among you of lineage, and likewise messengers are sent through the lineages of their people. I asked you, did any of you say this?

He accepted it and she stated that no. So I said: If someone had said this before him, I would have said that he is a man taking inspiration from a statement that was said before him. I asked you: Were any of his fathers kings? So I mentioned that no, so I said, “If there had been among his fathers someone who had kingship,” I said, “A man seeking his father’s kingdom.” I asked you: Were you accusing him of lying before he said what he said? So I mentioned that no, because I know that he would not have lied to people and lied to God. I asked you: Did the noblest people follow him or the weak among them? So you mentioned that the weak among them followed him, and they were the followers of the messengers. And I asked you: Are they increasing or decreasing?

So you mentioned that they increase, and so does the matter of faith until it is completed. And I asked you: Does anyone apostatize out of discontent with his religion after he enters into it? So you mentioned that no, and so is faith when it mixes with hearts on its screen, no one displeases it. And I asked you: Does he betray? You said no, and likewise the messengers do not betray. And I asked you: What does he command you to do?

So you mentioned that he commands you to worship God and not associate anything with Him, and forbids you to worship idols, and commands you to pray And honesty and chastity. If what you say is true, then he will possess the place where my feet are. I knew that he was outside, and I did not think that he would be Of you, if I knew that I would be sincere to him, I would strive to meet him, and if I were with him, I would wash his feet.

Then he called for the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which he had sent with Dihya al-Kalbi to the chief of Busra, and the chief of Busra sent him to Heraclius read it and found in it:

“In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, from Muhammad, the servant of God and His Messenger, to Heraclius, the Great of Rome, peace be upon whoever follows guidance. As for what follows, I invite you With the call to Islam, accept Islam and you will be safe. Submit. May God give you your reward twice. If you turn back, then upon you is the sin of the Arisians, and {O people The Book: Come to a common word between us and you, that we worship none but Allah, and do not associate anything with Him, and do not take one another as lords. Instead of Allah, then if they turn away, then say, “Bear witness that we are Muslims.” [Al Imran: 64] »

Abu Sufyan said: When he said what he said and finished reading the book, the noise increased and the voices rose and we were sent out, so I said To my companions when we were expelled: The matter of Ibn Abi Kabshah is very bad. The king of Banu al-Asfar fears him, so I am still certain that he will appear until... God brought Islam to me.

Ibn al-Natur, the companion of Elijah, a bishop for the Christians of the Levant, used to say that when Heraclius came to Elijah, he became an evil person one day. Then some of his wits said to him: We disapproved of your appearance. Ibn al-Natur said: Heraclius was a mourner looking at the stars, and he said to them when they asked him: “I saw tonight when I looked at the stars that the king Circumcision has appeared, so who among this nation is circumcised? They said:

Only Jews are circumcised, so do not worry about them. Write to the cities of your kingdom and let them kill any of the Jews among them, for while they are on the verge of Their order, Heraclius brought a man sent by the King of Ghassan to inform about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When Heraclius informed him, he said: Go and see whether he is circumcised or not? So they looked at him and told him that he was circumcised, and he asked him about the Arabs. He said: They are circumcised, so Heraclius said:

This king of this nation has appeared. Then Heraclius wrote to a friend of his in Rome. Heraclius was his equal in knowledge, and Heraclius walked. To Homs until a letter came to him from his companion agreeing with Heraclius’ opinion regarding the departure of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

He said hello and that he was a prophet, so Heraclius gave permission for the Roman leaders to attack him in Homs, then he ordered its gates to be closed, then he looked at them. Then he said: O people of the Romans, is it possible for you to achieve prosperity and maturity, and for your kingdom to be established and for you to follow this prophet? They found the doors closed, so when Heraclius saw their repulsion and despaired of their faith, he said: Return them to me, and he said: I said My article above was to test your strength in your religion, as I saw that they prostrated to him and were satisfied with him, so this was the last matter of Heraclius.

I said: Heraclius was one of the leaders of the Christian kings at that time, and more than one person told us that this book has survived to this day. The descendants of Heraclius are in the highest flint and the most honorable place, inheriting it from generation to generation, and more than one person reported that this book remains to this day. Al-Fansh, the owner of Castile and Andalusia, is proud of him, and this is a famous and well-known matter.

Sunaid, who is the sheikh of Al-Bukhari, narrated in his interpretation, saying: Hisham told us, he said: Husayn told us on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad bin Al-Hadi, he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to Heraclius, and he read his letter, and the Romans gathered, but they refused. He said: When he On Sunday, their senior bishop did not show up and he pretended, so he sent to him but he refused. Then he sent to him but he refused three times, so he rode to him and said: To him: Didn't you know that he is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: Yes, he said:

Have you not seen what they rode from me? You are more obedient to them than I am, so come and call them. He said: And give me permission in that. He said: Yes. He said: Go, he. When he came, he said: So he brought his black man to their great church, and when they saw him, they fell down and prostrated before him, the king and others, and he stood at the altar and said: Oh The sons of the dead, this is the prophet whom Jesus preached about, and I bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, so they bowed down and jumped up. Then they bit him with their mouths until they killed him. He said: And they took out his ribs with two bitches until he died.

chapters.title: Sending him as a messenger to the King of Egypt, Muqawqas, the Christian king
paragraphs: [Sending him as a messenger to the King of Egypt, Muqawqis, the King of the Christians]

Chapter: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, also sent a messenger to the King of Egypt, Muqawqis, the king of the Christians at that time in Alexandria. And his messenger to him was Hatib bin Abi Balta’ah, may God be pleased with him. Hatib said: I came to Al-Muqawqis - whose name is Jarih bin Mina - with a letter from the Messenger of God. God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so I said to him: Before you there was a man who claimed that he was the Most High Lord, so God punished him for the hereafter and the first. So take revenge on him, then take revenge on him, so take care of someone else and he will not take care of you. He said: Bring it. I said:

Indeed, you have a religion that you will not abandon except for what is better than it, and that is Islam, which is sufficient after everything else. Indeed, this prophet called people to God, and it was The strongest against him were the Quraysh, the Jews prepared them for him, and the closest to him were the Christians. For my life, the good news of Moses about Jesus is nothing but the good news of Jesus. By Muhammad, and We have not called you to the Qur’an except as you call the people of the Torah to the Gospel, and everyone who recognizes a prophet is from his nation, for the truth is They must obey him, for you are one of those who met this prophet, and we do not forbid you from the religion of Christ, but we command you to do so.

Then he handed him the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and when he read it he said: Good. I looked into this and found that he does not enjoin anything that is false in it or He forbids what is desired, and I did not find him to be a misguided magician or a false soothsayer, but I found with him the instrument of prophecy. Then he put the letter in an ivory case, sealed it, gave it to his treasurer, and wrote his answer to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: I have learned. Indeed, a prophet has remained, and I have honored your messenger.

He presented as a gift to the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, two maidservants and a mule called Al-Duldal. The Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, accepted his gift and chose the maid. One, whose name was Mariah al-Qibtiyyah, was for himself, and she bore him Ibrahim, and he gave the other to Hassan ibn Thabit, and she bore him Abdul Rahman, and the mule lived until the time of Muawiyah, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The evil person feels jealous of his kingdom, and his kingdom will not last.”

Muhammad bin Saad said: Muhammad bin Omar told us, he said: Abd al-Hamid bin Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned Peace be upon him from Al-Hudaybiyyah, in Dhul-Qa’dah in the sixth year of the Hijra. Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah sent to Al-Muqawqis Al-Qibti, the companion of Alexandria and wrote to him with a letter inviting him to Islam. When he read the letter, he said to him:

Good, and he took the letter, and it was sealed, and he put it in an ivory pouch and sealed it, and gave it to his treasurer, and wrote to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He answered his letter, but he did not surrender, and he presented as a gift to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, what was mentioned above.

Each of the two kings venerated the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and humbled himself before him and his book, and acknowledged that he was the Awaited Messenger who The prophets, peace be upon them, announced it.

Al-Muqawqis knew that he was true based on what he heard about his characteristics from the People of the Book, but he was disillusioned with his kingdom and did not believe, and he had left Al-Mughirah was brought to him before Al-Mughirah converted to Islam, so he told him about that.

Muhammad bin Omar Al-Waqidi said: Muhammad bin Saad Al-Thaqafi, Abdul-Rahman bin Abdul-Aziz, Abdul-Malik bin Issa, and Abdullah told me. Ibn Abd al-Rahman and Muhammad Ibn Yaqoub Ibn Utbah, on the authority of his father and others, each of them narrated a portion of this hadith to me, saying: Al-Mughirah bin Shu’bah said about his going out to Al-Muqawqis with Bani Malik, and when they entered Al-Muqawqis, he said: How did you get rid of me? Your sect and Muhammad and his companions between me and you? They said: We stuck to the sea and we were afraid of it because of that. He said: How did you do what he called you to?

They said: Not a single man among us followed him. He said: Why is that? They said: He brought us a new religion that our fathers did not follow, nor did the king follow, and we are following what our fathers followed. He said: So how did his people do? They said: Their younger ones followed him, and those behind him from his people and other Arabs met him in places where there was a circle, and sometimes there was For him. He said: Don't you tell me what he is calling for? They said: They call us to worship God alone, with no partner, and to renounce what the forefathers worshiped, and they call to prayer and zakat. He said:

What about prayer and zakat? Do they have a known time and a number to which they will end? They said: They pray five prayers today and tonight, all of them for specific times and a number that they have named.

And they paid half a mithqal from every wealth that amounted to twenty mithqals, and they informed him of the charity of all the wealth. He said: Have you seen when he takes it, where does he put it? They said: He returns it to their poor, and he commands the upholding of ties of kinship and fulfillment of covenants, and the prohibition of adultery and alcohol, and he does not eat of anything slaughtered to anyone other than God. Al-Muqawqis said:

This is a prophet sent to the people, and if he had succeeded the Copts and the Romans, they would have followed him, and Jesus, son of Mary, had commanded them to do so, and this is the one from whom you are describing. The prophets before him were sent with him, and the outcome will be for him so that no one will dispute with him and his religion will be demonstrated to the utmost in concealment and discretion. He was cut off by the seas, and his people were about to attack him with spears. They said: If all the people had entered with him, we would not have entered. Al-Mughirah said: Al-Muqawqis lowered his head and said: You are in the game, then he said: What is his lineage among his people? We said: He is the middle of them in lineage. He said:

Likewise, the Messiah and the prophets were sent in the lineage of their people. Then he said: How was his hadith? He said: We said: He is called nothing but trustworthy because of his truthfulness. He said: Look into your matter. Do you think he is telling the truth in what is between you and him and lying about God? He said: Who followed him? We said: events. He said: They and Christ are followers of the prophets before him. He said what she did

Are the Jews of Yathrib the people of the Torah? We said: They disagreed with him, so he attacked them, killed them and took them captive, and they dispersed in every direction. He said: They are an envious people who envied him, but do they not know about him as we do? Al-Mughirah said: So we got up from him, and we had heard words that subjugated us to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we submitted to him and said: The kings of the Persians. They believe him and fear him because they are close to him, and we are his relatives and neighbors and did not enter with him even though he came calling us to our homes. Al-Mughirah said:

So I returned to our house and stayed in Alexandria, not leaving a church without entering it, and I asked its bishops, both Copts and Greeks, about They find the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. There was a Coptic bishop who was the head of the church of John. They used to bring their patients to him, and he would pray. I have never seen someone more diligent than him, so I went to him and said: Is there any of the prophets left? He said:

Yes, he is the last of the prophets. There is no one between him and Jesus, son of Mary, and he is a sent prophet. Jesus commanded us to follow him, and he is the prophet. The illiterate Arab is named Ahmed. He is neither tall nor short. He has red eyes, and he is neither white nor of human age. He combs his hair and wears something He thickened his clothes and was covered with what

He finds food, his sword is on his shoulder, and he does not care who he meets. He begins the fight himself, and his companions are with him, and they sacrifice themselves for him. They are his. He has greater love than their children and their parents. He leaves a sacred land and comes to a sacred land. He migrates to a land of marshes and palm trees. He follows the religion of Abraham. Peace be upon him. Al-Mughirah said: So I said to him: Add more to me in his description. He said:

He girdles his waist, washes his extremities, and specializes in things that were not specific to the prophets before him. The Prophet was sent to his people, and he himself was sent to all people, and the earth was made for him as a place of mosque and purification. Whenever prayer led him, he performed tayammum. He prayed, and those before him were strict about them not praying except in churches and shops. Al-Mughirah bin Shu’bah said: I understood all of that from what he said and the words of others, and what I heard from that.

Al-Waqidi narrated a long hadith about his return and conversion to Islam, and what he was told of about the qualities of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that was something that amazed the Prophet. May God bless him and grant him peace, and he loves his companions to hear him. Al-Mughirah said: I used to tell them about that, and this is a matter known to the scholars of the People of the Book and their great figures.

Abu Hatim narrated in his Sahih, on the authority of Amr ibn Al-Aas, that he said: An army of Muslims - I am their commander - went out until we camped. Alexandria, and one of their great men said: Bring out to me a man who will speak to me and I will speak to him. I said: Let no one but me come out to him. He said: So I went out. My interpreter came to him and with me, and his interpreter was with him. He said: What are you? So I said:

We are the Arabs, we are the people of thorns, and we are the people of the Sacred House of God. We were the narrowest of people in terms of land, and the most difficult of them to survive. We eat dead things. And blood, and we attacked each other, until a man came out among us, neither the greatest of us at that time, nor the most wealthy among us, and he said, “I am the Messenger of God to you.” So he commanded us to do what we did not know, and forbade us to do what we were doing, and our fathers were doing, so we denied him and refuted what he said, until a people came out to him. He changed us and fought us and defeated us and defeated us, and he turned to the Arabs next to him and fought them until he defeated them. If only the Arabs behind me knew what There is no one left who does not come to you to share with you in the life you are in.

He laughed, then said: Indeed, your Messenger has spoken the truth. Our messengers have brought to us something similar to what your Messenger brought, so if you take the matter Your Prophet, no one will fight you except that you defeat him, and no one will partner with you unless you defeat him, even if you do the same as we did and leave the matter Your Prophet, you were not greater in number than us, nor were you more powerful than us.

chapters.title: Chapter on his fight, may God bless him and grant him peace, the Christians
paragraphs: [Chapter: His, may God bless him and grant him peace, fighting the Christians]

Then, after sending to the kings, he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, began to invade the Christians, so he first sent Zayd bin Harithah and Ja’far bin Abi Talib. Abdullah bin Rawaha was in an army, and they fought the Christians with a martyr from the land of Karak, and he said to his companions:

Your prince is Zaid. If he is killed, then Ja`far, and if he is killed, then Abdullah bin Rawahah. The three were killed, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed of the killing of The three on the day they were killed, and it was reported that Khalid ibn al-Walid had taken the banner, so God granted victory at his hands. Then, after this, he invaded The Christians himself, and he ordered all the Muslims to go out with him in the raids, and he did not allow anyone to remain behind him, and he fought in dozens of Thousands of people invaded Tabuk, so he came to Tabuk and stayed there for twenty nights. To attack the Christians, their Arabs, Romans, and others, and he waited for them to fight them, but they heard about him and refrained from fighting him, but did not They approach him.
And God Almighty revealed the most beautiful Surah (Al-Bara’ah) in that regard, and He Almighty condemned those who neglected the jihad of the Christians with great condemnation.

And those who did not see their struggle as obedience, He made them hypocrites and disbelievers. God will not forgive them if they do not repent, and He said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he said: “It is the same to them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them - God will never forgive them” [Al-Munafiqun: 6].
And God Almighty said: “And do not pray for any of them who has died, nor stand at his grave” [At-Tawbah: 84].

So if this is what God and His Messenger said to you regarding those who neglected their jihad because he did not see it as obedience and did not see it as obligatory, then what is his ruling regarding them? themselves? Until God Almighty said: {Say: If your fathers and your sons and your brothers and your wives and your kindred and the wealth you have acquired and your trade... You fear its stagnation, and dwellings with which you are pleased are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His cause, so wait until Allah brings about His command.} [Repentance: 24].
Then upon his death, may God bless him and grant him peace, he ordered us to expel the Jews and Christians from the Arabian Peninsula.

In Sahih Muslim: Omar bin Al-Khattab said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: “I will expel the Jews and Christians from the island of Arabs until I do not leave anyone but a Muslim.”

Imam Ahmad and Abu Ubaid narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The last thing the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke. He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Expel the Jews of Hijaz and the Christians of Najran from the Arabian Peninsula.”

His successors, may God be pleased with them, rose after his religion, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, so Abu Bakr al-Siddiq sent armies; Because of the Christians’ invasion of the Levant, several invasions took place between the Muslims and themselves, and Abu Bakr died while they were besieging Damascus, then Omar bin Al-Khattab conquered the whole of the Levant, Egypt, Iraq and some of Khorasan during his caliphate, and he came to the Levant during his caliphate and the Christians handed over to him the House of The holy one because of its characteristic they saw.

Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Aidh said in the book Al-Futuh, he said: Ata’ Al-Khorasani said: When the Muslims descended on the Holy House, he said to them Their leaders: We have gathered to reconcile with you, and you have recognized the location of Bayt al-Maqdis and that it is the mosque to which your Prophet was taken captive. We would love for your king to open it - and the Caliph was Omar bin Al-Khattab - so the Muslims sent a delegation, and the Romans also sent a delegation with... The Muslims until they came to Medina, and they began to ask about the Commander of the Faithful. The Romans said to their translators: Who are they asking? They said:

On the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, their astonishment intensified, and they said: This is the one who defeated Persia and the Romans, and took the treasures of Chosroes and Caesar, and he has no known place. With it! With this, he defeated the nations, and they found him sleeping while the heat hit him, and their astonishment increased. When he read Abu Ubaidah’s letter, he approached until He camped at Jerusalem and there were twelve thousand Romans and fifty thousand people of the land, so he reconciled with them, and among the reconciliation was that Not one of the Jews should enter upon them. Then he entered the mosque and found
